question: The planes $\frac{x}{2}+\frac{y}{3}+\frac{z}{6}=1$ and $\frac{x}{3}-\frac{y}{2}+\frac{z}{6}=1$ intersect in space. Determine both the acute and obtuse angles between the two planes.
explanation:
Conversion to Cartesian Form
Multiplying the first equation by $6$ gives
$$3x+2y+z=6$$
Hence, a normal vector to the first plane is
$$\vec{n_1}=3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}$$
Multiplying the second equation by $6$ gives
$$2x-3y+z=6$$
Hence, a normal vector to the second plane is
$$\vec{n_2}=2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+\hat{k}$$

Applying the Formula
If $\theta$ is the acute angle between the planes, then
$$\cos\theta=\frac{|\vec{n_1}\cdot\vec{n_2}|}{|\vec{n_1}||\vec{n_2}|}$$
Now,
$$\vec{n_1}\cdot\vec{n_2}=3(2)+2(-3)+1(1)=1$$
Also,
$$|\vec{n_1}|=\sqrt{9+4+1}=\sqrt{14}$$
and
$$|\vec{n_2}|=\sqrt{4+9+1}=\sqrt{14}$$
Therefore,
$$\cos\theta=\frac{1}{14}$$
Hence, the acute angle is
$$\theta=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{14}\right)$$
The other angle between the planes is supplementary to the acute angle. Therefore, it is
$$180^\circ-\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{14}\right)$$

Final Result
The acute angle is $\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{14}\right)$ and the obtuse angle is $180^\circ-\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{14}\right)$.
